More Weather Changes For The AI Supply Chain

Will Denyer, Tan Kai Xian

Gavekal Research | 17 Nov 2026

The artificial intelligence investment environment continues to change rapidly in the wake of the US midterm elections and the romantic affairs of Nvidia’s former chief executive, Jensen Huang. These two developments are already starting to affect domestic permitting, export controls and financing. Most recently, the US Commerce Department announced tighter export controls on US chips Monday, as one of Huang’s affairs has increased scrutiny of the various loopholes Chinese companies have used to gain direct or indirect access to Nvidia’s advanced AI chips (see The Nvidia Blast Zone). At the same time, the US government is preparing a list of “national champions” that will receive expedited export licenses.The challenge for investors is to assess the risks and opportunities these changes present for different parts of the AI supply chain.
